questions.knowledgeNote: A relation X→Y is a function iff every element of X has exactly one image in Y — one output each, no element left without an image.
questions.question: Q1(a). Let X = {a,b,c}, Y = {p,r,s}. Is R1 = {(a,p),(a,r),(b,r),(c,s)} a function from X to Y? Give reason.
questions.solution: Check each element of X: a appears twice — (a,p) and (a,r), i.e. a has two images p and r. A function allows exactly one image per domain element. ✅ NOT a function (a violates uniqueness).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q1(a)

questions.knowledgeNote: Totality matters too: every domain element must appear at least once as a first component.
questions.question: Q1(b). With X, Y as above, is R2 = {(a,p),(b,r)} a function? Give reason.
questions.solution: List first components: {a, b} — element c ∈ X has no pair, so no image for c. A function from X to Y must cover all of X. ✅ NOT a function (c has no image).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q1(b)

questions.knowledgeNote: Many-to-one is allowed: distinct domain elements may share one image; only one-image-per-element and full coverage are required.
questions.question: Q1(c). With X, Y as above, is R3 = {(a,s),(b,s),(c,s)} a function? Give reason.
questions.solution: First components: a→s, b→s, c→s. Every element of X appears exactly once as a first component. ✅ IS a function (constant function; many-to-one is legal).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q1(c)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same test: each of a, b, c used exactly once ⇒ function, even though a and b share image p.
questions.question: Q1(d). With X, Y as above, is R4 = {(a,p),(b,p),(c,s)} a function? Give reason.
questions.solution: a→p, b→p, c→s — all three domain elements covered exactly once. ✅ IS a function.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q1(d)

questions.knowledgeNote: One-to-one onto a 3-element codomain subset: each domain element used once ⇒ function (bijective onto {p,r,s}).
questions.question: Q1(e). With X, Y as above, is R5 = {(a,p),(b,r),(c,s)} a function? Give reason.
questions.solution: a→p, b→r, c→s — every element of X has exactly one image. ✅ IS a function.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q1(e)

questions.knowledgeNote: Inverse by interchange: set y = f(x), swap to x = …, then solve for y.
questions.question: Q3(a). Find a formula for the inverse function f⁻¹ if f: R→R, f(x) = x + 1.
questions.solution: Step 1 — Let y = x + 1. Step 2 — Interchange: x = y + 1. Step 3 — Solve: y = x − 1. ✅ f⁻¹(x) = x − 1. (Check: f(f⁻¹(x)) = (x−1)+1 = x ✔)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q3(a)

questions.knowledgeNote: Linear inverse: after swapping, isolate y by undoing ×2 then −3.
questions.question: Q3(b). Find f⁻¹ if f: R→R, f(x) = 2x + 3.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q3(b)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same template with constant 5: y = (x−5)/2.
questions.question: Q3(c). Find f⁻¹ if f: R→R, f(x) = 2x + 5.

questions.knowledgeNote: Cubic inverse uses the real cube root: x = y³+5 ⇒ y = ∛(x−5).
questions.question: Q3(d). Find f⁻¹ if f: R→R, f(x) = x³ + 5.
questions.solution: Step 1 — y = x³ + 5. Step 2 — x = y³ + 5. Step 3 — y³ = x − 5, so y = ∛(x−5). ✅ f⁻¹(x) = ∛(x−5). (Check: (∛(x−5))³+5 = x ✔)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q3(d)

questions.knowledgeNote: gof means apply f first: g(f(x)) = 3(2x+1)−1.
questions.question: Q4(a-i). Let f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = 3x − 1. Find gof(x).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q4(a) gof

questions.knowledgeNote: fog reverses the order: f(g(x)) = 2(3x−1)+1. Order matters — compare with gof.
questions.question: Q4(a-ii). With f, g as above, find fog(x).
questions.solution: fog(x) = f[g(x)] = f(3x−1) = 2(3x−1) + 1 = 6x − 2 + 1. ✅ fog(x) = 6x − 1. (Note gof ≠ fog here.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.2 Q4(a) fog
